title: Does last year’s cancer reinstatement prevent this year’s fracture reinstatement, and does the same-member 15-day gap still apply?

customer.contract: Synthetic accepted Health Ensure policy using preserved UIN BAJHLIP24149V062324
customer.selected_options: Reinstatement option premium paid and accepted
customer.past_event: The same insured used reinstatement for cancer in the prior policy year. The current fracture is explicitly not cancer or kidney failure requiring regular dialysis.
customer.current_usage: Base SI and all cumulative bonus completely exhausted by a registered and paid earlier claim; no reinstatement used in current policy year.
customer.benefit_scope: Subsequent otherwise admissible inpatient fracture claim; not the exhaustion-producing claim.

conversation.text: I used the cancer reinstatement last year. Is reinstatement unavailable forever, even for my new fracture?
Is the option accepted this year, has the base plus bonus been exhausted by paid claims, and is this a later admission for you or another member?
Yes, selected and paid. The earlier paid claim exhausted both. This is my later fracture admission, after discharge on 1 August. It is planned for 15 August.

The clause limits cancer and defined kidney-failure reinstatement to once in the insured’s lifetime but separately allows yearly reinstatement for other admissible conditions. That does not remove the same-member gap: 15 August is only 14 elapsed days after 1 August.
The hospital corrects the later admission date to 16 August.

That is 15 elapsed days and meets the stated at-least-15-day gate on these synthetic dates. Keep the prior cancer-use history and current-year exhaustion separately. This is not approval of the fracture claim or restoration of unrelated sublimits.

known: Base plus bonus exhausted by registered and paid claim
unknown: Actual accepted schedule and complete governing bundle
Clinical classification and all current claim admissibility/amount inputs

corrections.effect: Recompute only the elapsed-gap predicate and dependent conclusion; do not erase the former proposed date.

candidate_dispositions.status: Annual condition-frequency and corrected date gates satisfied under stipulations; actual payment unestablished

expected_answer: Do not apply a cancer-specific lifetime restriction to every condition. For this other-condition claim, annual availability still depends on paid option, qualifying SI, exhausted base plus bonus, subsequent-claim status, one-use-per-year scope and same-member minimum 15-day gap. The corrected date reaches that gap. A different insured is explicitly exempt from this 15-day period; that is not an exemption from all other conditions.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent conditional explanation of both frequency scopes and the corrected date, withholding actual settlement.

title: Can the Health Care Supreme Plan A total of INR 642500 all fund a hospitalization?

customer.configuration: Synthetic accepted Plan A using the exact preserved Health Care Supreme table, UIN BAJHLIP23210V042223
customer.usage: No earlier use and no bonus or other extra cover stipulated
customer.source_interpretation: The page’s Plan A label is known; its visually ambiguous grouping into Vital is not assumed.

conversation.text: My Plan A row shows total sum insured 642500. Can that all pay my 600000 hospital bill?
Does the row separate hospitalization from OPD, physiotherapy, maternity, donor, air ambulance and recovery benefits?
Yes. The hospitalization column is 500000; the other columns are 2500, 5000, 25000, 50000, 50000 and 10000.

Those columns sum to 642500, but the hospitalization pool in this row is 500000. The separate components cannot be swept into it just because the display adds them. The gross difference between your stipulated 600000 hospitalization and that pool is 100000, before any other applicable adjustments. Actual payout requires the complete schedule and terms.

title: Which Golden Shield room rule applies when the same wording contains A and B inpatient structures?

customer.requested_room: Single private AC room at INR 7500 per day
customer.missing_configuration: No schedule or product benefit table identifying whether A or B inpatient structure applies

conversation.text: Golden Shield allows a single private AC room at my 1000000 SI, correct?
Please identify the inpatient structure selected in your schedule or benefit table. This exact wording contains both A and B structures.
I only have this wording. Page 10 says single private AC at 10 lakh, while page 11 shows 6000 per day at 10 lakh.

Both passages exist. A states the category rule; B states the monetary grid. I cannot pick one from the product name or combine them into a more generous rule. The 7500 room exceeds B’s 6000 daily grid by 1500 if B applies, but that counterfactual does not establish your controlling room rule or all claim deductions.
